answers.answer: Each player chooses a color and stands that color's Player ID card visibly in front of them. Give each player the matching-color Voting card set, remove cards targeting colors not in play, and keep their own Ambush card. Deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center with values hidden.
answers.evidence: Setup: stands the Player ID card visibly in front; remove cards targeting colors not playing; deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center.

answers.answer: There is no player-by-player turn order. A player may change their face-down Voting card choice until cards are revealed. Once everyone has chosen, all choices are revealed simultaneously.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: There is no individual turn order. Vote: change the chosen card until cards are revealed; reveal simultaneously.

answers.answer: No four-vote majority is required. Red is the Target because Red received the most votes; the highest vote total determines the Target, even if it is only a plurality. Here Red's three votes exceed Blue's and Green's two each.
answers.evidence: Vote: The player receiving the most votes is the Target.

answers.answer: Both Red and Blue are Targets because they tie for the most votes. With neither using Ambush, both are eliminated. A player may survive the voting requirement by having voted for either tied Target.
answers.evidence: If several players tie for the most votes, all of them are Targets; with tied Targets, voting for any one satisfies the voting requirement.

answers.answer: No. Green is eliminated because Green did not vote for the sole Target, Blue. Receiving no votes does not keep Green alive.
answers.evidence: Every other player who did not vote for any Target is also eliminated.

answers.answer: Among the stated cards, Red's Ambush is not a vote; Yellow's vote for Red and Pink's vote for Yellow each count as one. Red and Yellow tie for most votes, so both are Targets. Red's Ambush succeeds and Red may eliminate one player who voted for Red: Yellow. Pink voted for a Target (Yellow), so Pink survives; Red survives through the successful Ambush. Thus Red and Pink survive, and Yellow is eliminated, assuming the listed votes are the complete vote.
answers.evidence: Ambush cards do not count as votes; tied leaders are all Targets. A successful ambusher chooses one player who voted for them to eliminate. With tied Targets, voting for any one satisfies the voting requirement.

answers.answer: No. A successful Ambush eliminates exactly one player who voted for that ambusher. They may not choose someone who voted for another color instead.
answers.evidence: The ambusher chooses one of the players who voted for them; they cannot choose an arbitrary player or someone who voted for a different Target.

answers.answer: The player eliminates themselves. An Ambush works only if its player is a Target; otherwise it fails.
answers.evidence: An Ambush played by someone who is not a Target fails: that player eliminates themselves.

answers.answer: No gold is awarded yet. With four survivors, the players continue with another Conspire and vote among the survivors.
answers.evidence: Three or more survivors: continue with another conspiracy and vote among survivors.

answers.answer: The sole survivor collects all four central Gold Bar cards. Those are four cards, not four points; each card is worth 3, 4, or 5 points.
answers.evidence: One survivor collects all four central Gold Bars. A bar is a card whose value is 3, 4, or 5 points.

answers.answer: They resolve a Final Showdown for the central Gold Bars. Each takes a set of three cards—Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go—may discuss intentions and a bargain, then each chooses one card and places it face down. When both are ready, they reveal simultaneously.
answers.evidence: Each takes Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go; they may discuss, choose one face down, then reveal simultaneously.

answers.answer: Each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar card from the deck. Players who participated in that final vote receive no consolation bar for this outcome, including those eliminated in it. Nobody collects the four central bars; leave all four in the center for the next round and add no new bars.
answers.evidence: With none surviving, each player not participating in the final vote receives one bar. Leave the four central bars for next round; add no new bars.

answers.answer: Each finalist receives two Gold Bar cards.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown Share/Share: each gets 2.

answers.answer: The Share finalist gets zero central bars; the Steal finalist gets all four.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown Share/Steal: Share gets 0; Steal gets 4.

answers.answer: The Grab One & Go finalist gets one central bar; the Steal finalist gets three.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown Grab One & Go/Steal: Grab One & Go gets 1; Steal gets 3.

answers.answer: The Grab One & Go finalist gets one central bar; the Share finalist gets three.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown Share/Grab One & Go: Share gets 3; Grab One & Go gets 1.

answers.answer: Each finalist takes one central bar. Two bars remain in the center, and if play continues, deal just two new bars for the next round.
answers.evidence: Each finalist receives one central bar; leave two in the center and add just two new bars for the next round.

answers.answer: Neither finalist receives gold. Every other player receives one Gold Bar card from the deck. Leave all four central bars for the next round and add no new gold to the central pool.
answers.evidence: If both choose Steal, neither finalist receives gold; every other player gets one deck bar; leave all four central bars for next round.

answers.answer: Check for victory at the end of the round, after Gold Bars are awarded, regardless of how the round ended. With 6–9 players the threshold is at least 25 points; with 10–12 players it is at least 24 points. If multiple players qualify with different totals, the player with the highest point total wins.
answers.evidence: Check victory at end of round after bars are awarded; 25 points with 6–9 players, 24 with 10–12; highest point total wins.

answers.answer: If exactly two qualifying players tie for the highest Gold point total, they conduct another Final Showdown; continue until one player has the highest total. If a normal round ends without a winner, everyone returns, including players eliminated during that round.
answers.evidence: Tied totals: the tied players conduct another Final Showdown until one player has the highest total. If no winner, everyone returns.
